title: Structuring the three acts: Beginning, Middle, and End
text: Them here? Middle: Challenges, learning, real contributions. End, growth, impact, and where they go next. plus a soft invite for the reader. Three objectives every post. Highlight a real journey. Show how volunteering builds skills and confidence. Encourage current and former volunteers to be seen. Thank. Prove.

title: Picking the right arc (Save the Cat, Alumni Breakthrough)
text: Recruit. Same. Three jobs as the profile system now with a full arc. Not every journey uses the same flavor. Match the person to an arc so the series never feels copa- paste. Current volunteer still in progress. Save the cat. Alumni breakthrough, rags to riches. Returned

title: The Consent Ladder: Navigating privacy from full names to pseudonyms
text: Home with new knowledge, voyage, and return. Overcame a hard challenge. Overcoming the monster. Consent comes first. Always offer a ladder, not a yes or no trap. Full name, first name only, pseudonym, role only, or fully anonymous. You do not need a face to tell the story. Treat the work as the asset. Stay specific. Anonymous never means vague. Why anonymity still works?

title: Why anonymous stories still build trust and credibility
text: More people say yes. It protects job searches, visas, family. Focus lands on what was built. And trust still holds. A real quote and a real result are proof. A name is not what makes it credible. So lock this takeaway. Beginning, middle, end, match the ark. Ask consent. Publish

title: Recap: Spine, arc, consent, and rhythm
text: On a rhythm. The people keep doing new things so the calendar stays full without inventing drama. Your turn. Pick one volunteer you know. Write their three acts in six lines total. Then choose a privacy level from the latter before you draft the public post. The three-act volunteer story. Your takeaway, spine, arc, consent, rhythm.
